data.name: Maximiliana
data.gender_notes: Maximiliana is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Maximiliana is a Latin name derived from the elements maxima (greatest) and ilianus (of Ilia). The name is composed of the prefix 'max-' which means 'greatest', and the suffix '-iliana' which refers to a woman. The name is a feminine form of Maximilian and is associated with strength, power, and leadership. In Christian tradition, the name is also associated with Saint Maximilian Kolbe, a Polish Conventual Franciscan friar, who is known for his great acts of heroism and self-sacrifice.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strong, powerful, and self-sacrificing women.

in_greek.name: Μαξιμιλιανᾶ
in_greek.meaning: ἡ ὑψηλή, ἡ βασιλίσσα, ἡ τὰ θαύματα ἔχουσα
in_greek.long_meaning: Μαξιμιλιανᾶ ἐστὶ ὄνομα Ἑλληνικόν, ὃ δὲ σημαίνει 'ἡ ὑψηλή' ἢ 'ἡ βασιλίσσα', ἀναφερόμενον εἰς τὴν νηπιακὴν ἐξέτασιν τοῦ ὀνόματος. Παράλληλα, τοῦτο ὄνομα συνδέεται μέ τὸ Μáξιμιλιανóς, ἀρρενοὺς ὄνομα, ὃ σημαίνει 'ὁ μέγας' ἢ 'ὁ πλούσιος'. Ἐν τῇ Νεοτέτῃ Ἀνατολικῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ, τὸ ὄνομα Μáξιμιλιανᾶ ἐν τῇ φιλομαθείας ὕψει τοῦ ὀνόματος. Ἡ χρήση του ὑπάρχει ἰστορικά ἐν τῇ χριστιανικῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ, ὡς ὑπενθύμιση εἰς τὴν ὑψηλότητα καὶ τὴν βασιλίδωσιν τοῦ Θεοῦ. Τὸ ὄνομα ὑποδηλώνει ἰδιότητας ὡς: ὑψηλότητα, βασιλίδωσιν, τὰ θαύματα ἔχουσα, καὶ ἀπάντηση.

in_latin.name: Maximiliana
in_latin.meaning: forma divina, regina, habens miracula, magnificus, bonus
in_latin.long_meaning: Maximiliana est nomen Latinum, quod significat 'forma divina' vel 'regina', quae refertur ad interpretationem Christiana nominis. Nomen hoc connectitur cum Maximiliano, nomen masculinum, quod significat 'magnus' vel 'dives'. In Ecclesia Christiana, nomen Maximiliana est in usu historicus, ut indicatio ad dignitatem et regalitatem Dei. Nomen hoc potest denotare qualitates quae sunt: dignitas, magnificus, bonus, et libertas.

historical_references.reference: Maximiliana of Austria was the eldest daughter of Emperor Maximilian I and his wife, Mary of Burgundy. She was born on January 31, 1483, and was named after her grandfather, Maximilian, Duke of Burgundy. Maximiliana became the heir to the Duchy of Burgundy upon her father's death in 1494, but she was only nine years old at the time. Her mother, Mary, acted as regent until Maximiliana came of age in 1506.

historical_references.reference: Maximiliana of Austria (1505-1574) was a member of the House of Habsburg and the Duchess of Parma from 1521 until her death in 1574. She was the daughter of Emperor Maximilian I and his wife, Anna of Bohemia and Hungary. Maximiliana was named after her grandmother, Maximiliana of Burgundy, who was a significant figure in the power struggles between the Burgundian and Habsburg dynasties during the late 15th century.
